rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line uses كاد for nearly doing an act, supporting a non-redundant reading of أكاد.
rows.anchor: هممت ولم أفعل وكدت وليتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following al-Naḥḥās, he ends the preceding sentence and takes أكاد أخفيها as a fresh report that God conceals the Hour.
rows.anchor: وتم الكلام ثم استأنف الإخبار بأنه يخفيها واختاره النحاس

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group reads أكاد أخفيها من نفسي as indicating how obscure the Hour is to creatures; this is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: معناه أكاد أخفيها من نفسي

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Others gloss من نفسي as from my own initiative and from me.
rows.anchor: ولما رأى بعضهم قلق هذا القول قال معنى من نفسي

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: A group, with this sense also reported from Ibn Jubayr, treats أكاد as extra and says God hides the Hour’s time; the cited proofs do not establish that reading.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة أكاد زائدة لا دخول لها في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that the cited Qur’anic and poetic examples prove كاد is semantically redundant.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة في شيء من هذا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God almost conceals the Hour entirely, but disclosed its coming while veiling its time for the benefit of warning.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أكاد أخفيها فلا أقول هي آتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects I nearly hide it from Myself as an ellipsis unsupported by contextual evidence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أكاد أخفيها من نفسي ولا دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ubayy and other codex additions, including a reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh, are hyperbolic Arabic expressions for intense concealment, not literal divine ignorance.
rows.anchor: وهذا محمول على ما جرت به عادة العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخفيها refers to the Hour, which is the Resurrection Day without disagreement; السعي means deeds.
rows.anchor: والضمير في أخفيها عائد على الساعة والساعة يوم القيامة بلا خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in عنها وبها apparently refer to the Hour; another view takes them as prayer, while a remote view refers عنها to the prior profession of divine oneness.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في عنها وبها عائد على الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in فلا يصدنك is apparently to Moses; a prohibition need not imply that an infallible prophet could actually do the forbidden thing, since its practical audience may be another hearer.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب في فلا يصدنك لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers it remote that the wording addresses the Prophet while meaning his community.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لفظا ولأمته معنى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers two rhetorical readings: forbidding the unbeliever to turn Moses away signals that Moses must not disbelieve, or the unbeliever’s turning away results from Moses’ weakness, so the result signals its cause.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: العبارة أنهى من لا يؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتردى may be subjunctive under the prohibition or indicative, then you will fall; Yaḥyā reads it with a kasra on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: فتردى يجوز أن يكون منصوبا على جواز النهي وأن يكون مرفوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s question about the staff draws Moses’ attention to the miracle: God already knows what it is, but will transform dry wood into a moving serpent and display His power.
rows.anchor: وقد علم تعالى في الأزل ما هي وإنما سأله ليريه عظم ما يخترعه عز وجل في الخشبة اليابسة من قلبها حية نضناضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, ما is the subject, تلك its predicate, and بيمينك a circumstantial phrase governed by the demonstrative.
rows.anchor: وما استفهام مبتدأ وتلك خبره وبيمينك في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows تلك to function as a relative pronoun meaning that which is in your right hand; Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentions this alone, but the author says this is a Kufan, not Basran, analysis.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون تلك اسما موصولا

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق والجحدري
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Jaḥdarī read عصي, replacing the alif with yāʾ and assimilating it to the first-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق والجحدري عصي بقلب الألف ياء وإدغامها في ياء المتكلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads عصاي with kasra on the yāʾ, also transmitted from Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr; the kasra resolves two adjacent quiescent letters.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن عصاي بكسر الياء وهي مروية عن ابن أبي إسحاق

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق والجحدري
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq and al-Jaḥdarī are also reported to read عصاي with a quiescent yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي إسحاق والجحدري عصاي بسكون الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أتوكؤا means leaning on the staff while walking or standing; Moses adds useful detail beyond the direct answer, as in Prophetic answers that add a benefit.
rows.anchor: أتوكؤا عليها أي أتحامل عليها في المشي والوقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added detail reflects Moses’ desire to prolong intimate conversation with God and its delight, gratitude for the staff’s benefits, and a move from two specific uses to general purposes.
rows.anchor: وحكمة زيادة موسى عليه السلام رغبته في مطاولة مناجاته

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet wishes to prolong reproach because its conversation is pleasurable, illustrating Moses’ desire to extend his colloquy.
rows.anchor: وأملى عتابا يستطاب فليتني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes أتوكؤا an answer to a second, unstated question about what Moses does with the staff.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أتوكؤا عليها جواب لسؤال آخر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God asked both what the object was and what Moses held in his right hand, with the staff’s uses answering the latter.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سأله تعالى عن شيئين عن العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects that analysis: بيمينك is not a question, and Moses first mentions his own benefit, then the benefit to his flock.
rows.anchor: وفي التحقيق ليس قوله بيمينك بسؤال

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: The majority read وأهش with ḍamma on hāʾ and shīn; al-Nakhaʿī reads it with kasra, with the same sense and an omitted object, leaves.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وأهش بضم الهاء والشين المعجمة

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل
rows.claim: Abū al-Faḍl allows a root meaning to bend foliage or grass toward the flock while tending it.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل ذلك أن يكون من هش يهش هشاشة إذا مال

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima read وأهس with unpointed sīn, meaning to drive the flock.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعكرمة: وأهس بضم الهاء والسين

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khālawayh attributes to al-Nakhaʿī a quadriliteral reading وأهس with a hamza bearing ḍamma.
rows.anchor: ونقل ابن خالويه عن النخعي أنه قرأ وأهس بضم الهمزة من أهس رباعيا

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ reports from ʿIkrima and Mujāhid a softened-shīn reading, apparently avoiding doubled shīn because its frication is heavy.
rows.anchor: وذكر صاحب اللوامح عن عكرمة ومجاهد وأهش بضم الهاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reports al-Nakhaʿī’s quadriliteral form with ḍamma on hamza and shīn; both roots evoke brittle bread crumbling.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري عن النخعي أنه قرأ وأهش بضم الهمزة والشين المعجمة من أهش رباعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses lists ordinary benefits because he senses an extraordinary event is coming; the miracle will eclipse every use he has just named. The stick was called nabʿa.
rows.anchor: ذكر على التفصيل والإجمال المنافع المتعلقة بالعصا كأنه أحس بما يعقب هذا السؤال من أمر عظيم يحدثه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group reads غنمي with a quiescent nūn; another vocalizes the construction so the verb acts directly on the flock.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة غنمي بسكون النون وفرقة على غنمي بإيقاع الفعل على الغنم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators list practical uses: the forked stick and hook bend or break branches, carry gear, provide shade, extend a short rope, and protect the flock from predators.
rows.anchor: والمآرب ذكر المفسرون أنها كانت ذات شعبتين ومحجن فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account attributes further miracles to the staff: drawing water, changing its forks to a bucket or lights, fighting enemies, bearing fruit, following Moses with provisions, producing springs, guarding against vermin, and gathering distant sheep.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان فيها من المعجزات أنه كان يستقي بها فتطول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The staff was said to come from the prophetic staffs kept with Shuʿayb, brought from Paradise by Adam, and to measure ten cubits; another report gives twelve cubits by Moses’ measure.
rows.anchor: وهذه العصا أخذها من بيت عصي الأنبياء التي كانت عند شعيب حين اتفقا على الرعية هبط بها آدم من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although مآرب is plural, أخرى is feminine singular as if the plural were one feminine noun; this is allowed generally and better suits the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وعامل المآرب وإن كان جمعا معاملة الواحدة المؤنثة فأتبعها صفتها في قوله أخرى ولم يقل آخر رعيا للفواصل

rows.speaker: الزهري وشيبة
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī and Shayba are reported to read مارب without a fully articulated hamza, apparently easing it between vowel qualities.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وشيبة: مارب بغير همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to throw the staff is God’s; saying an angel spoke by God’s permission is remote. ألقها means cast it down.
rows.anchor: قال ألقها الظاهر أن القائل هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited idiom describes someone casting down a staff and settling, illustrating ألقاها.
rows.anchor: فألقت عصاها واستقر بها النوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic word for snake covers small and large, male and female; جان is slender and ثعبان large, so the descriptions are compatible: it grew, or was likened to a slender snake for its speed.
rows.anchor: والحية تنطلق على الصغيرة والكبيرة والذكر والأنثى والجان الرقيق من الحيات والثعبان العظيم منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One description gives the serpent a horse-like crest, the staff’s forks as its fangs, and forty cubits between its jaws.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان لها عرف كعرف الفرس وصارت شعبتا العصا لها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the transformed serpent swallowing rocks and trees, with the hook like a neck and its eyes glowing.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: انقلبت ثعبانا تبتلع الصخر والشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ fear was a human response to a terrible, mind-shaking sight; تسعى means moving and walking quickly.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى هذا الأمر العجيب الهائل لحقه ما يلحق البشر عند رؤية الأهوال والمخاوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miracle occurs during the colloquy to accustom Moses to its terror before confronting Pharaoh and to train him for prophetic burdens; God then orders him to pick it up and not fear.
rows.anchor: وحكمة انقلابها وقت مناجاته تأنيسه بهذا المعجز الهائل حتى يلقيها لفرعون فلا يلحقه ذعر منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Moses feared the serpent because he knew what Adam had suffered from it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما خافها لأنه عرف ما لقي آدم منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another says Moses became so reassured by God’s command that he put his hand into its mouth and took it by the beard.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما قال له الله لا تخف بلغ من ذهاب خوفه

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī’s account says God had to command Moses to take the snake repeatedly before he obeyed on the third command.
rows.anchor: ويبعد ما ذكره مكي في تفسيره أنه قيل له خذ مرة وثانية حتى قيل له خذها ولا تخف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects Makkī’s account as unfitting for a prophet to disobey his Lord’s command twice.
rows.anchor: لأن منصب النبوة لا يليق أن يأمره ربه مرة وثانية فلا يمتثل ما أمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once Moses took the serpent in his hand, it became a staff again; سيرة comes from walking and extends to mean a way or manner, as the cited poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: وحين أخذها بيده صارت عصا والسيرة من السير كالركبة والجلسة

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī parses سيرتها as a second object of سنعيدها with an omitted preposition, or as a substitute for the object.
rows.anchor: فقال الحوفي مفعول ثان لسنعيدها على حذف الجار مثل واختار موسى قومه

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows سيرتها to substitute for the object as an explanation of its quality and manner.
rows.anchor: وقال هذا الثاني أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses سيرتها as an adverb meaning in its former manner, when it was a staff; the author objects that this fixed adverb needs a preposition, omitted only rarely or poetically.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: يجوز أن ينتصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also derives the construction from عاد بمعنى رجع إليه, which takes two objects; al-Ḥawfī had given this as his first analysis.
rows.anchor: وعادك أن تلاقيها عداء فيتعدى إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers a third parse: سنعيدها stands independently for restoring the staff after it disappeared through transformation; سيرتها is an understood verbal clause, ‘moving along its former way.’
rows.anchor: ووجه ثالث حسن وهو أن يكون سنعيدها مستقلا بنفسه غير متعلق بسيرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جناح literally means a bird’s or angel’s wing, then extends to arm, side, and an army’s flank; it is called a wing because a bird inclines with it.
rows.anchor: والجناح حقيقة في الطائر والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told to press his hand against his side beneath the upper arm, calming him and displaying the hand miracle; its emergence entails an unstated taking-out, clarified by the parallel command to insert his hand in his collar.
rows.anchor: والمراد إلى جنبك تحت العضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hand emerges shining white like the sun, unlike Moses’ ordinary complexion. Sūʾ means badness or ugliness and euphemistically denotes leprosy, which Arabs loathed.
rows.anchor: تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء قيل خرجت بيضاء تشف

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī treats من غير سوء as an adjective describing the white hand, governed by an understood state of being.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: من غير سوء في موضع النعت لبيضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من غير سوء is rhetorical qualification preventing white from implying leprosy or a skin patch.
rows.anchor: ويقال له عند أرباب البيان الاحتراس لأنه لو اقتصر على قوله بيضاء لأوهم أن ذلك من برص أو بهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آية may be a circumstantial accusative for those who permit multiple states for one referent; another parse supplies made it or gave you a sign.
rows.anchor: وانتصب آية على الحال وهذا على مذهب من يجيز تعداد الحال لذي حال واحد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows an omitted command خذ before آية, but the author rejects his alternative دونك because an imperative noun cannot lose both its agent and governed object.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون منصوبا على إضمار خذ ودونك وما أشبه ذلك حذف لدلالة الكلام

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥawfī allow آية as apposition to بيضاء; Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows it as a state of the pronoun in بيضاء.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء والحوفي أن يكون آية بدلا من بيضاء وأجاز أبو البقاء أن يكون حالا من الضمير في بيضاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse supplies a deleted verb: We made it a sign or gave you a sign.
rows.anchor: وقيل منصوب بمحذوف تقديره جعلناها آية أو آتيناك آية

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī connects the purpose-lām in لنريك to اضمم or تخرج.
rows.anchor: واللام في لنريك قال الحوفي متعلقة باضمم

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ connects the lām to the omitted verb ‘made/gave it a sign’ or the implied meaning ‘We demonstrated by it.’
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: تتعلق بهذا المحذوف يعني المقدر جعلناها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī sees the hand as an additional sign after the staff and parses لنريك as taking either الكبرى or من آياتنا as its second object, with الكبرى describing the signs.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لنريك أي خذ هذه الآية أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers من آياتنا as the second object and الكبرى as its adjective: this makes the signs themselves great and avoids the singular superlative describing both miracles.
rows.anchor: والذي نختاره أن يكون من آياتنا في موضع المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the hand is a greater miracle than the staff because he takes الكبرى as the second object referring to the nearby hand; the author rejects this since the staff entails more transformations.
rows.anchor: ويبعد ما قال الحسن من أن اليد أعظم في الإعجاز من العصا لأنه ذكر عقيب اليد لنريك من آياتنا الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff is greater: it changes form and size, gains life, power, and limbs, swallows vegetation and stone, then becomes a staff again, while the hand merely changes color.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس في اليد إلا تغيير اللون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing the miracles, God sends Moses to Pharaoh because he transgressed; Pharaoh is singled out as the head of disbelief and claimant to divinity, with his people as followers.
rows.anchor: أمره بالذهاب إلى فرعون رسولا من عنده تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid relates that Moses’ tongue defect came from the ember he put into his mouth: after Moses pulled Pharaoh’s beard (or struck him), Gabriel turned his hand from a jewel to a coal, burning his tongue.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كانت من الجمرة التي أدخلها فاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire affected Moses’ tongue rather than his hand, refuting those who explain events by natural properties alone.
rows.anchor: وإحراق النار وتأثيرها في لسانه لا في يده دليل على فساد قول القائلين بالطبيعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses had a lisping or stammering defect.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس كانت في لسانه رتة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the speech impediment arose after Moses’ colloquy so that he would not speak to anyone afterward.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حدثت العقدة بعد المناجاة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub describes Moses’ condition as a speech impediment.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب: كانت فيه مسكة عن الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā equates the knot with stammering and repeating sounds.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عيسى: العقدة كالتمتمة والفأفأة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say Moses asked only for enough relief to be understood, with some defect left, citing Aaron’s greater eloquence and the claim that Moses scarcely spoke clearly.
rows.anchor: وطلب موسى من حل العقدة قدر ما يفقه قوله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the knot was fully removed because God granted Moses’ request; the author says asking for a knot means one knot, not the entire speech defect.
rows.anchor: وقيل: زالت لقوله قد أوتيت سؤلك يا موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects reading ولا يكاد يبين as actual inability to speak, since Pharaoh and his people understood Moses; Pharaoh said it deceptively, perhaps meaning Moses gave no proof.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك فرعون تمويها وقد خاطبه وقومه وكانوا يفهمون عنه فكيف يمكن نفي البيان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says Moses first states his need generally, then specifies chest and task, making the petition more emphatic than direct wording through summary followed by detail.
rows.anchor: قد أبهم الكلام أولا فقال اشرح لي ويسر لي فعلم أن ثم مشروحا وميسرا ثم بين ورفع الإبهام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the indefinite العقدة requests only enough resolution for comprehension, not perfect eloquence; من لساني describes the knot, as al-Ḥawfī also says.
rows.anchor: وفي تنكير العقدة وإن لم يقل واحلل عقدة لساني أنه طلب حل بعضها إرادة أن يفهم عنه فهما جيدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One etymology derives وزير from burden: a king’s minister bears the ruler’s loads and expenses.
rows.anchor: والوزير المعين القائم بوزر الأمور أي بثقلها فوزير الملك يتحمل عنه أوزاره ومؤنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another derives وزير from refuge, supported by a couplet about shelter from predatory beasts but no shelter from people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الوزر وهو الملجأ يلتجىء إليه الإنسان

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī derives وزير from mutual assistance; al-Zamakhsharī says the expected form would be أزير and posits hamza-to-wāw change supported by comparable forms.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: هو من المؤازرة وهي المعاونة والمساعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the need to posit a hamza shift: derivation from burden is straightforward, while يوازر reflects a non-obligatory change after a preceding ḍamma.
rows.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى ادعاء قلب الهمزة واوا لأن لنا اشتقاقا واضحا وهو الوزر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Grammarians offer several object parses for appointing a minister: لي and وزيرا as two objects, or وزيرا and هارون, with هارون as apposition in the first analysis.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون لي وزيرا مفعولين لا جعل وهارون بدل أو عطف بيان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows هارون as clarifying apposition; the author finds this unlikely because apposition usually proceeds from the less famous name to the better known one, opposite this order.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وإن جعل عطف بيان آخر جاز وحسن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse takes وزيرا من أهلي as the two objects, with لي completing the meaning, while retaining the previous analysis of هارون.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون وزيرا من أهلي هما المفعولان ولي مثل قوله ولم يكن له كفوا أحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some supply an omitted command meaning bring Aaron near; the author sees no need because the sentence is complete.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن ينتصب هارون بفعل محذوف أي اضمم إلي هارون وهذا لا حاجة إليه لأن الكلام تام

rows.speaker: الحسن وزيد بن علي وابن عامر
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Ibn ʿĀmir read اشدد with fatḥa on hamza and أشركه with ḍamma as a jussive imperfect answering the request.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وزيد بن علي وابن عامر اشدد بفتح الهمزة وأشركه بضمها فعلا مضارعا مجزوما على جواب الأمر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another reading attributed to al-Ḥasan uses the intensive verb شدد, asking for repeated strengthening whenever difficulty arises.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح عن الحسن أنه قرأ أشدد به مضارع شدد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the forms as commands of supplication for strength and for Aaron to share the prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور اشدد وأشركه على معنى الدعاء في شد الأزر وتشريك هارون في النبوة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir’s command asks for Aaron’s practical assistance and shared governance, not shared prophethood, which Moses cannot assign.
rows.anchor: وكان الأمر في قراءة ابن عامر لا يريد به النبوة بل يريد تدبيره ومساعدته

rows.speaker: مصحف عبد الله
rows.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh includes أخي before اشدد.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله أخي واشدد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: For the imperative reading, al-Zamakhsharī parses أخي as a subject and اشدد به as its predicate, pausing after هارون; the author says this is contrary to the apparent reading and unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز فيمن قرأ على لفظ الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron was four years older than Moses.
rows.anchor: وكان هارون أكبر من موسى بأربعة أعوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses presents the requested blessings as means for worship, diligence, and mutual cooperation, which increase desire for good.
rows.anchor: وجعل موسى ما رغب فيه وطلبه من نعم سببا تلزم منه العبادة والاجتهاد في أمر الله والتظافر على العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God free of what is unbefitting; it precedes remembrance and praise because purification concerns the heart, while spoken praise concerns the tongue.
rows.anchor: وقدم التسبيح لأنه تنزيهه تعالى في ذاته وصفاته

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats كثيرا as modifying an omitted verbal noun or as a circumstantial phrase, meaning in a state of abundant glorification.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا نعت لمصدر محذوف أو منصوب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنك كنت بنا بصيرا means God knows their circumstances; سؤل is the thing requested, like bread and eating for what is baked and eaten, and God granted the requests including Aaron’s ministry.
rows.anchor: والسؤل فعل بمعنى المسئول كالخبز والأكل بمعنى المخبوز والمأكول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recounts an earlier favor to spur Moses to diligence and confidence; مرة أخرى means a different favor, not a later or second favor in sequence.
rows.anchor: ومرة معناه منة وأخرى تأنيث آخر بمعنى غير أي منة غير هذه المنة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand God’s inspiration to Moses’ mother as inspiration of intuition, like inspiration to the bees.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور: هي وحي إلهام كقوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes it communication through a dream or angel without prophethood; the author prefers this as the apparent sense, citing the promise to return Moses and make him a messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وحي إعلام إما بإراءة ذلك في منام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests inspiration through a prophet at the time, like inspiration to the disciples; the author considers this remote because no prophet is reported in Pharaoh’s era.
rows.anchor: ويبعد ما صدر به الزمخشري قوله: من يرد يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ما يوحى creates suspense and is explained as the command to place Moses in the ark.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله ما يوحى إبهام وإجمال كقوله إذ يغشى السدرة ما يغشى فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم وفيه تهويل وقد فسر هنا بقوله أن اقذفيه في التابوت

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats أن as explanatory because الوحي means speech; Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats it as a source-forming particle in apposition to ما, and the author accepts both analyses.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وأن هي المفسرة لأن الوحي بمعنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark was apparently made of wood; reports instead describe reed, plugged holes, leather or cotton lining, and plaster and pitch.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن التابوت كان من خشب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yamm means a sweet-water sea or specifically the Nile; the author favors the broader reading because Pharaoh’s people were drowned in it, not in the Nile.
rows.anchor: وألقته في اليم وهو اسم للبحر العذب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in the command to cast him into the sea and what follows refer to Moses, the topic; the ark is only the container and incidental mention.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في فاقذفيه في اليم عائد على موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya makes the first pronoun refer to Moses and the second to the ark, while allowing both to refer to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والضمير الأول في اقذفيه عائد على موسى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says all pronouns refer to Moses to avoid dividing them between him and the ark, which would disrupt the Qur’anic composition.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والضمائر كلها راجعة إلى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although proximity normally favors the nearer antecedent, the pronoun returns to the discourse topic rather than an incidental object; he rebuts Ibn Ḥazm’s use of proximity to make the prohibition apply to all pig parts instead of pork flesh.
rows.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول إن الضمير إذا كان صالحا لأن يعود على الأقرب وعلى الأبعد كان عوده على الأقرب راجحا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ولتصنع with kasra on lām, ḍamma on tāʾ, and an accusative verb; it means Moses was raised and treated well, watched with care.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ولتصنع بكسر لام كي وضم التاء ونصب الفعل أي ولتربى ويحسن إليك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda gives a similar sense: God watched over and cared for Moses as a person watches something attentively.
rows.anchor: وأنا مراعيك وراقبك كما يراعي الرجل الشيء بعينيه

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās reads صنع as making the horse splendid or treating it well, and connects the clause to a suppressed cause or to a following verb.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: يقال صنعت الفرس إذا أحسنت إليه

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو نهيك
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Abū Nuhayk open the tāʾ; Thaʿlab explains it as Moses’ movement and conduct occurring under God’s eye.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو نهيك بفتح التاء

rows.speaker: شيبة وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Shayba and one transmission from Abū Jaʿfar read an imperative with quiescent lām and ʿayn; another transmission from Abū Jaʿfar has a kasra on lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ شيبة وأبو جعفر في رواية بإسكان اللام والعين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A narrative says Moses’ sister Maryam tracked the rejected infant, brought his mother to nurse him, and cleverly presented the family as eager to serve the queen; his mother stayed home, and the royal household rewarded them and later presented Moses to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: قيل اسمها مريم سبب ذلك أن آسية عرضته للرضاع فلم يقبل امرأة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya links إذ تمشي to an understood ‘We favored you’ verb; al-Zamakhsharī links it to ألقيت or تصنع, or makes it a substitute for إذ أوحينا.
rows.anchor: والعامل في إذ قال ابن عطية فعل مضمر تقديره ومننا إذ.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defends making the walk a substitute for the inspiration by comparing events at different times within one broad year; the author rejects this because the moments here are narrowly specified and cannot overlap.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بدلا من إذ أوحينا فإن قلت:

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attaches إذ to تصنع, or permits an understood command meaning remember.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: إذ متعلقة بتصنع

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read كي تقر with fatḥa on tāʾ and qāf; a group kasrates qāf, both dialect forms; Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh reads a passive form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور كي تقر بفتح التاء والقاف.

rows.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
rows.claim: Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh reads تُقَرَّ with ḍamma on tāʾ and fatḥa on qāf, in the passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جناح بن حبيش بضم التاء وفتح القاف مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The murdered man was the Copt whom an Israelite asked Moses to help against; Moses was twelve and feared God’s punishment and Pharaoh’s reprisal, then was forgiven after asking and saved by flight to Midian.
rows.anchor: وقتلت نفسا هو القبطي الذي استغاثه عليه الإسرائيلي قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghamm is distress weighing on the heart through fear or lost aims; although a Quraysh dialect uses it for killing and others link it to the ark or sea, the author prefers the killing because Moses was taken from Egypt to Midian.
rows.anchor: والغم ما يغم على القلب بسبب خوف أو فوات مقصود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses الفتون as being delivered from successive trials; examples include the infant massacre, the river, Pharaoh’s threat, killing a Copt, hired service, losing the way, and sheep scattering in darkness.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس خلصناك من محنة بعد محنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الفتون is a plural verbal noun for trials and ordeals; God tested Moses and delivered him until he was fit for prophethood.
rows.anchor: والفتون مصدر جمع فتن أو فتنة على ترك الاعتداد بالتاء كحجوز وبدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an gives Moses ten years in Midian; Wahb says twenty-eight including the dowry, with eight stages of travel, ten years tending Shuʿayb’s sheep, then eighteen married years until age forty, the customary prophetic age.
rows.anchor: والسنون التي لبثها في مدين عشر سنين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على قدر means at an appointed time, neither earlier nor later; another explanation takes it as the forty-year interval at which prophets receive revelation.
rows.anchor: على قدر أي وقت معين قدرته لم تتقدمه ولم تتأخر عنه.

none: Verse text only; no commentary or distinct claim is given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a lexical note, اذهب في كلاءة الله and اكتلأت mean to be guarded and to take precautions; Ibn Hurma’s line witnesses يكلؤها.
rows.anchor: اذهب في كلاءة الله واكتلأت منه احترست.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: النفخة is glossed as a step; نفخ له من عطاياه means a portion of gifts sufficed him, with a cited poem as evidence.
rows.anchor: النفخة: الخطوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خردل is the familiar mustard seed.
rows.anchor: الخردل: حب معروف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ is Meccan without disagreement.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية بلا خلاف

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh counts al-Kahf, Maryam, Ṭā Hā, and al-Anbiyāʾ among the earliest suras he learned, an old, accumulated portion of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله: الكهف، ومريم، وطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura answers Quraysh’s reaction to the preceding warning of reckoning: they said Muhammad’s promised resurrection and judgment were false or far off, so God revealed that their reckoning had drawn near.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة هذه السورة لما قبلها أنه لما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اقترب has the basic sense of قرب, though some consider it more emphatic because of its augmented form; الناس may mean Meccan polytheists or all deniers of resurrection.
rows.anchor: واقترب افتعل بمعنى الفعل المجرد وهو قرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The approaching reckoning means the Hour’s time; حساب can mean measuring an amount or the amount counted. What is coming is near despite a long wait, near to God, or near relative to the shorter future than past.
rows.anchor: واقتراب الحساب اقتراب وقته والحساب في اللغة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says he and the Hour were sent like these two fingers, indicating nearness; a poet similarly says the hoped-for one is nearer than tomorrow and the feared one farther than yesterday.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «بعثت أنا والساعة كهاتين»

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says للناس either attaches directly to اقترب or emphasizes that the reckoning belongs to them; the author rejects the second as unattested and syntactically problematic.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هذه اللام لا تخلو من أن تكون صلة لاقترب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He objects that the possession-emphasis analysis has no recognized parallel here, lacks a governor if attached to the genitive source, and should follow the emphasized phrase; لَأبا لك is exceptional and not a model.
rows.anchor: فلا نعلم أحدا يقول ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw in وهم is circumstantial. Their heedlessness and turning away are compatible: they fail to consider consequences, then ignore reminders when awakened from inattention.
rows.anchor: والواو في وهم واو الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الذكر is the Qur’an revealed in successive portions; another view takes it as the Prophet’s legal teachings, exhortations, and reminders.
rows.anchor: والذكر هنا ما ينزل من القرآن شيئا بعد شيء.

rows.speaker: بعض الصحابة
rows.claim: Asked about محدث, a Companion answered that the Qur’an is newly descended and newly uttered.
rows.anchor: وسئل بعض الصحابة عن هذه الآية فقال محدث النزول محدث المقول

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl takes الذكر to mean the Prophet, as the next accusation calls him human; he cites the verse saying God sent down a reminder, a messenger.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن بن الفضل: المراد بالذكر هنا النبي

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites use محدث to argue that the Qur’an is originated; the author notes this is a theological debate.
rows.anchor: وقد احتجت المعتزلة على حدوث القرآن بقوله محدث وهي مسألة يبحث فيها في علم الكلام

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read محدث in the genitive as an adjective agreeing with ذكر by form; Ibn Abī ʿAbla has nominative by syntactic position, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī an accusative circumstantial; من ربهم may attach to يأتيهم.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور محدث بالجر صفة لذكر على اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استمعوه is a circumstantial clause for the object of يأتيهم; وهم يلعبون describes the listeners, and لاهية modifies their play or adds a successive circumstance to their listening.
rows.anchor: واستمعوه جملة حالية وذو الحال المفعول في ما يأتيهم وهم يلعبون جملة حالية من ضمير استمعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لاهية derives from being distracted: even when people notice the reminder, heedlessness dominates their hearts; Ibn Abī ʿAbla and ʿĪsā read it nominative as a second predicate of وهم.
rows.anchor: واللاهية من قول العرب لهي عنه إذا ذهل وغفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: النجوى is private conversation by definition; أسروا means they intensely concealed it or made the consultation unnoticeable, though Abū ʿUbayda allows the opposite meanings hide and disclose.
rows.anchor: والنجوى من التناجي ولا يكون إلا خفية فمعنى وأسروا بالغوا في إخفائها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats أسروا as a contronym; al-Farazdaq’s line uses it for revealing what had been hidden, while al-Tabrīzī says it usually means concealment because conspirators guard secrets.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: أسروا هنا من الأضداد

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad makes الذين ظلموا a substitute for the plural marker in أسروا, condemning their wrongdoing; Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributes this to Sībawayh.
rows.anchor: فالرفع على البدل من ضمير وأسروا إشعارا أنهم الموسومون بالظلم الفاحش فيما أسروا به قاله المبرد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash take the wāw in أسروا as an explicit plural marker in the أكلوني البراغيث construction, a dialect some call rare and others sound, supported by poetry.
rows.anchor: والواو في أسروا علامة للجمع على لغة أكلوني البراغيث قاله أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī makes الذين the subject placed before أسروا as its predicate; the explicit noun replaces a pronoun to mark the group’s wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أو على أن الذين مبتدأ وأسروا النجوى خبره قاله الكسائي

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās chooses الذين as the subject of an omitted say, a common ellipsis supported by the following question هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم.
rows.anchor: واختاره النحاس قال ويدل على صحة هذا أن بعده هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes الذين ظلموا as an accusative of censure; another supplies أعني, while al-Farrāʾ makes it genitive as adjective or apposition to الناس, which the author calls the most remote analysis.
rows.anchor: والنصب على الذم قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم expresses amazement that Muhammad could be chosen as prophet despite being human, since they believed God sends only angels.
rows.anchor: استفهام معناه التعجب أي كيف خص بالنبوة دونكم مع مماثلته لكم في البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفتأتون السحر is a rebuke: they call the Qur’an and other miracles sorcery and ask how people can attend to it while seeing a human magician.
rows.anchor: السحر استفهام معناه التوبيخ والسحر عنوا به ما ظهر على يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two questions apparently belong to أسروا النجوى as its quoted secret speech; al-Zamakhsharī instead parses them as substitute for النجوى or attaches them to an omitted they said.
rows.anchor: وهاتان الجملتان الاستفهاميتان الظاهر أنهما متعلقتان

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ḥafṣ and other named readers read قال ربي as the Messenger’s report that God knows their words.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص والأعمش وطلحة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The rest of the seven read قل as a command to the Messenger to say God knows their words and requites them; speech includes public and secret words, exceeding a claim that He knows only their secrets.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة قل على الأمر لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objectors shift from calling revelation sorcery to confused dreams, fabrication, then poetry; this instability shows confusion. The statements may come from one group changing claims or from different factions.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى عنهم أنهم قالوا إن ما أتى به سحر ذكر اضطرابهم في مقالاتهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows the sequence to rank their assertions by increasing falsity, each later claim worse than the previous.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون تنزيلا من الله لأقوالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the poet accusation came from common people, since Arab poets recognized that the Qur’an is not poetry.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ثم حكى قول من قال إنه شاعر وهي مقالة فرقة عامية لأن بنات الشعر من العرب لم يخف عليهم بالبديهة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī reconstructs five evasions: human prophethood is impossible; conceding it, the Qur’an may be magic if beyond human eloquence, dreams if poor, fabrication if middling, or poetry if eloquent—none establishes a miracle.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: حكى الله عنهم هذه الأقوال الخمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand an overwhelming sign like earlier messengers, leaving no time for delay; the author notes this shows their knowledge that previous messengers brought signs.
rows.anchor: اقترحوا من الآيات ما لا إمهال بعدها كالآيات في قوله لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the comparison with earlier messengers is sound because sending messengers entails bringing signs.
rows.anchor: صحة التشبيه في قوله كما أرسل الأولون من حيث أنه في معنى كما أتى الأولون بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كما أرسل can modify آية, meaning a sign like earlier messengers’ signs, or an omitted noun for coming, meaning their coming with signs.
rows.anchor: والكاف في كما أرسل يجوز أن يكون في موضع النعت لآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested sign is a proposed one; God followed every proposed sign with punishment. He delayed punishment for Quraysh so they could survive and believe, and their words show awareness that earlier messengers received signs.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية التي طلبوها هي على سبيل اقتراحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier towns, such as the people of Ṣāliḥ and Pharaoh, were judged for destruction after proposing signs; they pledged to believe but reneged, so the rhetorical question denies these objectors would fare better.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم قوم صالح وقوم فرعون وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reply to the claim that a human cannot be a messenger, God says earlier messengers were men, not angels; Quraysh lacked scripture or prior learning and should ask learned authorities.
rows.anchor: ولما تقدم من قولهم هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم وأن الرسول لا يكون إلا من عند الله من جنس البشر قال تعالى رادا عليهم وما أرسلنا قبلك إلا رجالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أهل الذكر apparently means Jewish and Christian scriptural scholars: even opponents could not deny that God sent human messengers, so their testimony remains probative despite disbelief.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن أهل الذكر هم أحبار أهل الكتابين وشهادتهم تقوم بها الحجة في إرسال الله البشر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām says that he is among أهل الذكر.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن سلام: أنا من أهل الذكر

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī likewise says that he is among أهل الذكر.
rows.anchor: وقال علي: أنا من أهل الذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that أهل القرآن cannot mean Muslims at that time because they were the disputants.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: لا يصلح أن يكون المسئول أهل القرآن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other suggestions identify أهل الذكر as Qur’an scholars, Torah scholars, or historians of earlier nations; widespread transmission makes asking Jews and Christians valid.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أهل العلم بالسير وقصص الأمم البائدة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read يوحى passively; Ṭalḥa and Ḥafṣ read نوحي actively.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يوحى مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جسد may mean an inanimate, unnourished object or, by another definition, any bodily form; the latter reading makes the negation apply to the bodies’ property. Singular جسد denotes a class of bodies.
rows.anchor: والجسد يقع على ما لا يتغذى من الجماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebuts the objection that a messenger should not eat: human messengers were embodied, ate, and died; their messengership rested on miracles and protection from faults in conveying revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة من تمام الجواب للمشركين الذين قالوا هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم لأن البشرية تقتضي الجسمية الحيوانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s fulfillment of the prophets’ promise assures Muhammad and his companions of victory, giving believers a promise and disbelievers a threat.
rows.anchor: ذكر تعالى سيرته مع أنبيائه فكذلك يصدق نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه ما وعدهم به من النصر وظهور الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صدقناهم الوعد has a transitive construction that may omit a preposition, although this omission is not productive for most grammarians; the author lists parallels.
rows.anchor: وصدقناهم الوعد من باب اختار وهو ما يتعدى الفعل فيه إلى واحد وإلى الآخر بحرف جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ومن نشاء means believers; the profligates are disbelievers exceeding bounds, and the prophets were saved from enemies and their punishment.
rows.anchor: ومن نشاء هم المؤمنون، والمسرفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning the objectors, God names the Qur’an as a favor sent to them.
rows.anchor: ولما توعدهم في هذه الآية أعقب ذلك بوعده بنعمته عليهم فقال لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ذكر means their honor or renown, with a deleted possessive noun understood.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: ذكركم شرفكم حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says ذكر means their religion.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ذكر دينكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says ذكر means their account or mention.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد فيه حديثكم

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān takes it to mean their noble moral qualities and good works.
rows.anchor: وعن سفيان مكارم أخلاقكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation calls the Qur’an a reminder to avoid what is forbidden and pursue what is required.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تذكرة لتحذروا ما لا يحل

rows.speaker: صاحب التحرير
rows.claim: The author of al-Taḥrīr reads ذكر as a record of shameful acts and opposition to prophets, making the verse a rebuke rather than a list of favors and connecting it to their failure to reflect.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب التحرير: الذي يقتضيه سياق الآيات أن المعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows the honor/renown sense: the Qur’an preserves their name through time and urges them to consider its message.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: يحتمل أن يريد فيه شرفكم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī similarly reads ذكر as honor and lasting reputation, admonition, or noble virtues praised in the Qur’an, such as good neighborliness, loyalty, honesty, trust, and generosity.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري نحوه قال: ذكركم شرفكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rebutting the objectors, God intensifies the warning by recalling destroyed towns; town stands for inhabitants because a town itself cannot be unjust.
rows.anchor: لما رد الله تعالى عليهم ما قالوه بالغ تعالى في زجرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines إنشاء as bringing something into existence without a cause; the term also describes something newly arisen.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الإنشاء إيجاد الشيء من غير سبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قصم is severe breaking used for overwhelming destruction; كم signals multiplicity, so many towns’ inhabitants were destroyed violently.
rows.anchor: والقصم أفظع الكسر عبر به عن الإهلاك الشديد وكم تقتضي التكثير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the town as Ḥaḍūrā in Yemen; another relayed by Ibn Wahb from unnamed transmitters gives two Yemeni towns, examples rather than an exhaustive identification.
rows.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس أنها حضوراء قرية باليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ḥaḍūrā story says God sent a prophet whom the people killed; Nebuchadnezzar’s first two armies were defeated, but he won personally on the third campaign and they fled when killing began.
rows.anchor: ومن حديث أهل حضوراء أن الله بعث إليهم نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحسوا بأسنا means directly experiencing the punishment; the subject is the omitted town inhabitants, not the newly created people, who are given no reason to flee.
rows.anchor: فلما أحسوا بأسنا أي باشروه بالإحساس والضمير في أحسوا عائد على أهل المحذوف من قوله وكم قصمنا من قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in منها most likely refers to the town, but could refer to punishment as feminine in meaning severity; من marks cause. They fled on mounts as punishment advanced, or ran so quickly on foot that they were likened to riders.
rows.anchor: والضمير في منها عائد على القرية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Nebuchadnezzar’s men may taunt the fugitives to return for possible peace or tribute, then massacre them to avenge the murdered prophet; the account is transmitted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: يحتمل أن يكون من قول رجال بخت نصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the angels of punishment address inhabitants of destroyed towns generally: they thought they could bargain or defend themselves, but the angels taunt them as punishment overtakes them.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله: لا تركضوا إلى آخر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden reply after لما supports treating لما here as a particle rather than a temporal noun; the author says he discussed this earlier.
rows.anchor: وجواب لما إذا الفجائية وما بعدها
